@ziggertron yes! In the Extra Crisis mode—specifically in Dino Duel—alternate colors are assigned to Player 2 if both players select the same dinosaur species. While Player 1 typically uses the primary colors from the main game, Player 2 receives these specific variants: 
Velociraptor: Blue (often referred to as the Ultraraptor in certain versions).
Tyrannosaurus Rex: Black.
Allosaurus: White.
Triceratops: Gray.
Oviraptor: Orange-brown.
Compsognathus: Light green.

Regarding to the raptor, it is the only species with multiple variants in Dino Crisis 2. I found this info:

Main Story Color Variants:
While they all share the same basic model, their colors indicate their "Level" or difficulty:
-Brown (Level 1): The standard, weakest variant encountered at the start of the game.
-Green (Level 2): Feature green skin with orange/brown stripes; they are more resilient than the brown type.
-Swamp Green: A rare, lighter variant with black spots, though similar in strength to standard types.
-Red (Level 5): Encountered late-game (near the Missile Silo). They are significantly more aggressive and have much higher health than brown or green variants.
-Blue (Ultra-Raptor): The strongest non-boss enemy in the game. They only appear if you achieve a 20+ kill combo without taking damage and then enter a new raptor-infested area. They are extremely fast, resistant to hit-stun from the machete or stun gun, and can kill the player in just one or two hits. 

Extra Crisis (Dino Duel) Variants:
Dino Duel mini-game introduces even more colors for mirrors or specific unlocks:
Yellow: A unique variant often associated with specific challenges or the Dino Colosseum.
Black/Alternate Blue: Used primarily to distinguish between Player 1 and Player 2 in versus mode.
